key_insight: Magic state injections enable universal computation in transversal architectures while keeping sequential decoding volumes statistically bounded in the random circuits studied.
engineering_relevance: Sequential decoding could make large-scale fault-tolerant quantum circuits more tractable by limiting how much space-time syndrome data each measurement requires.
method: Construct decoding graphs by backpropagating logical measurement operators through transversal Clifford circuits with magic state injection.
Decode measurements sequentially, commit corrections, and exclude previously processed syndrome data.
Compare decoding volumes across measurement products, circuit connectivities, and Clifford gate ensembles.
evidence_signal: For random circuits, mid-circuit decoding volumes approach a stationary average governed by injection density, with exponentially suppressed large instances and similar qualitative behavior across the tested circuit variations.
watch_item: The abstract establishes decoding-volume behavior for random circuits, not end-to-end decoder runtime or accuracy on structured quantum algorithms.
paper_title: Bounded decoding complexity in transversal circuits with magic state injection
